items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Tuesday quashed criminal proceedings filed against a man accused of sexually harassing a woman after she came across him attending nature's call near a railway track. The complainant woman had accused the accused man of exposing his private parts to her and making certain inappropriate gestures at her. The Court, however, found that it appeared to be a case where the accused man had made some gestures out of shock when he found that the woman had seen him while he was urinating. Justice M Nagaprasanna opined that this cannot amount to the offence under Section 75 (2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), which deals with the offence of sexual harassment. The Court, therefore, allowed the accused man's plea to quash the criminal case against him. " The petitioner admittedly, even according to the complaint, was answering a nature's call ... after searching for a public toilet all over and not finding it ... The gesture that the complainant narrates is only a shock that the petitioner saw the complainant, as is narrated in the statement itself. That would not become in the considered view of this court an ingredient of outraging the modesty of a woman under Section 75(2). Permitting further proceedings at the case at hand on the aforesaid score would on the face of it become an abuse of the process of law and result in miscarriage of justice," it said. Justice M Nagaprasanna The 26-year-old accused man was travelling on a long-distance bus when the incident took place. He told the Court that he had de-boarded his bus to use the restroom. However, after he was unable to find a public toilet, he proceeded to relieve himself near a railway track. A 22-year-old woman was walking by when the accused man turned around. The woman claimed that in doing so, he exposed his private part to her and made gestures at her. She proceeded to file a criminal complaint against him for sexual harassment. Following a police investigation, the accused man was eventually charged for sexual harassment under Section 75 (2) of the BNS. A trial court also took cognisance of the case and summoned him for trial. The accused man proceeded to challenge these criminal proceedings before the High Court. The High Court today allowed his plea and quashed the case against him. Advocate Abhilash HS represented the petitioner (accused man) Advocate Swati Gopalkrishna appeared for the complainant.

items.title: MLA Mani C Kappan gets one-year jail term, fined Rs 1.2 crore in cheque-bounce case
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Pala MLA Mani C Kappan has been sentenced to one year of simple imprisonment by a Mumbai court in a cheque-bounce case linked to falsely promising shares in Kannur International Airport. The Additional Metropolitan Magistrate’s Court in Borivali also directed Kappan to pay Rs 1.20 crore as compensation to the complainant, along with 9% simple interest from the date of the order until the amount is realised. The court, presided over by Judge SA Khalane, convicted Kappan under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. He has been directed to pay the compensation within one month. Failure to do so will result in an additional three months of imprisonment. The court also directed the police to issue a non-bailable warrant for the execution of the sentence. The case was filed by Mumbai-based businessman Dinesh Menon who in 2019 had alleged that Kappan swindled him of Rs 3.5 crore after promising shares of Kannur International Airport (KIAL). The latest conviction comes after a series of legal proceedings involving Kappan. The Kerala High Court had earlier declined to interfere with the framing of charges against him in the case. However, a special court in Ernakulam subsequently acquitted Kappan of the criminal charges in February 2025. The Ernakulam court had dealt with the criminal proceedings arising from the same broader dispute. Kappan, a United Democratic Front MLA, has maintained that the case against him was politically motivated. He had also alleged that the case was intended to prevent him from taking up a ministerial position that he claimed had been promised to him. Sources close to Kappan said he will challenge the Mumbai court verdict before the appellate court.

items.title: NEET victim’s remembrance event held at Chennai beach despite police denying permission
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Around 50 members of the Anti-NEET Federation, led by S Maniratnam, brother of medical aspirant S Anitha, gathered at Besant Nagar beach in Chennai on Tuesday, September 1, to mark her ninth death anniversary, despite the police denying permission for the event. The gathering was held amid police security, with participants lighting candles, garlanding Anitha’s portrait and raising slogans against NEET. Speaking at the event, Manirathnam questioned the police’s decision to deny permission, saying the organisers had applied 15 days in advance for the remembrance programme. “Are we rowdies to pose a threat to public safety? This police reply indicates how the government looks at us. The government should make that clear,” Manirathnam said. He said the gathering would have been conducted on a larger scale if permission had been granted in time. Maniratnam also objected to the police describing the proposed event as a protest in its order. Around 50 members of the Anti-NEET Federation raised slogans against NEET. In its August 31 order, the police cited the Velankanni Matha Church festival in Besant Nagar, which is being held from August 29 to September 8. It said a large number of devotees from Chennai and other areas were expected to travel to the church by buses, vans, cars, and two-wheelers, as well as on foot. The police also cited the ongoing Devi Ellaiyamman temple festival in nearby Urur-Alcott Kuppam. The police said the proposed gathering could draw students and members of various student organisations and potentially cause disruption to vehicular movement and inconvenience to the public, affecting “law and order and public peace”. Also, in its September 1 order, the police cited the possibility of disruption but said the organisers could seek permission to hold a protest at designated locations including Sivanandam Salai and Panagal Maligai in Saidapet. Maniratnam said the organisers had sought permission for a remembrance meeting and not a protest or agitation.
